subject: City Council Hybrid Representation Subcommittee
overview: The committee established a subcommittee to research a hybrid ward-based representation model and adopted a new policy for real-time public participation during meetings.

items.title: Member Introductions
items.summary: The committee welcomed and introduced new members Paulette Van der Kloot, Phyllis Morrison, and Aubrey.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: Approved the minutes from the July 6 meeting.

items.title: Survey and Interview Status
items.summary: The chair reported the survey rollout is imminent, and members volunteered to conduct interviews with city department heads and former elected officials.

items.title: Public Participation Policy
items.summary: The committee approved a motion to disable the Zoom chat and allow two minutes of public comment after each agenda item, followed by a general three-minute comment period at the end of meetings.

items.title: City Council Composition Research
items.summary: Eunice Browne presented research showing that several city wards have had zero representation on the City Council since 2005.

items.title: Hybrid Representation Subcommittee
items.summary: Established a subcommittee to research the logistics, authority, and impacts of moving to a hybrid ward-and-at-large council system.

items.title: Focus Groups and Outreach Methodology
items.summary: Jean Zotter presented a plan to conduct five focus groups targeting populations often missing from city surveys, such as non-English speakers and residents with disabilities.

items.title: Event Planning and Listening Session
items.summary: The committee coordinated staffing for upcoming outreach events and scheduled a televised public listening session at City Hall for October 19.
